flashcards.a: DefaultMaxConnections=32 (lowered from 64), DefaultEFConstruction=128, search-time ef=-1 (dynamic: query_limit * dynamicEfFactor(8), clamped between dynamicEfMin=100 and dynamicEfMax=500).

flashcards.q: What does each HNSW knob (M, efConstruction, efSearch) cost when increased?
flashcards.a: M: more memory, slower build/search, better recall. efConstruction: slower build only (no query cost), better recall. efSearch: linearly more query latency, better recall, must be >= k.

flashcards.q: What is the HNSW memory formula and what does it give for 10M vectors at 768 and 1536 dims (M=16)?
flashcards.a: bytes/vector ~= 1.1*(4*dim + 8*M). At 768d: 3,520 B/vec -> 35.2 GB for 10M vectors. At 1536d: 6,899 B/vec -> 69.0 GB for 10M vectors.

flashcards.q: What is the IVF nlist rule of thumb, and what does nprobe control?
flashcards.a: nlist ~= sqrt(N) centroids (coarse k-means partition). nprobe = number of cells actually searched per query; directly trades recall for latency. Starting point: nprobe=8-16 for 1-10M vectors, tuned to recall plateau.

flashcards.q: How does product quantization (PQ) compress vectors, and what's the accuracy cost?
flashcards.a: Splits each vector into m subspaces, quantizes each against a codebook of 2^nbits centroids (typically nbits=8, 256 centroids), storing only the index -- e.g. 768d/m=96 -> 96 bytes vs 3072 bytes raw (~32x compression). Cost: quantization error is baked in at index time; no amount of nprobe tuning recovers it.

flashcards.q: What does ScaNN's anisotropic vector quantization do differently from plain PQ?
flashcards.a: Instead of minimizing uniform reconstruction error, it penalizes quantization error parallel to the database vector more heavily than error orthogonal to it, because parallel error is what actually shifts ranking under MIPS/dot-product similarity -- giving better recall-per-byte for ranking-sensitive tasks.

flashcards.q: What is DiskANN's Vamana graph and what performance does it achieve on SIFT1B?
flashcards.a: A single-layer (non-hierarchical) directed graph built via randomized init + two-pass alpha-pruning (~1.2). PQ-compressed vectors cached in RAM guide search; full vectors + graph live on SSD. On SIFT1B: 5000+ QPS, <3ms mean latency, 95%+ recall@1 on a 16-core/64GB-RAM machine.

flashcards.q: Why is filtered vector search genuinely hard?
flashcards.a: ANN indexes assume any indexed vector is a valid target. Pre-filtering degenerates to brute force over the filtered subset (no index over it). Naive post-filtering can under-return on selective filters because the unfiltered search never routed toward filter-valid regions of the graph.

flashcards.q: How does Weaviate's ACORN solve filtered search?
flashcards.a: Two-hop graph expansion so the search radius covers enough of the graph to find filter-valid neighbors regardless of selectivity; since v1.34 it's the default, auto-choosing between multi-hop exploration (selective filters), broader relaxed traversal (broad filters), or flat scan (tiny result sets).

flashcards.q: Can you cleanly delete a vector from an HNSW index?
flashcards.a: No -- deleted vectors are typically tombstoned, not physically removed (removing a node requires re-linking its neighbors, expensive to do online). Heavy churn degrades graph quality until a rebuild.
